comments.value:
I want to correct you on that:
"Udon is incredibly easy to use for people who know at least a little bit of programming"
This is _not_ true. I have years of experience, no issues programming in any other language and standard Unity C# is very easy for me, but Udon is a nightmare. It comes down to having zero documentation of what functions in Udon do or which functions are even whitelisted. It feels like VRChat doesn't want you to code and you have to reverse-engineer the game and eventually succeed after hours of frustration by randomly trying out stuff. VRChat documentation was always bad, but Udon documentation is non-existent.
Visual Studio / C# has an amazing capability of inline XML documentation, but Udon doesn't have any inline comments at all.
Basicly, the only way to survive right now is to use the search functions in Discord servers where people are all suffering together.

@{5c724f586a9e8a2255b7fc07|full_name}: I've started to realize this as well. My friend barely knows what he's doing and he's been basically trying to reverse engineer the whole thing by looking at compiled code to see what the nodes actually do in order to help me.

@{5cb0e62414ddd360bbe1ac29|full_name}: I just want to say, that there are some documentation areas. Furthermore, if you use UdonSharp, you can get code completion which further helps. UdonSharp even has a class tree browser which will tell you what's exposed or not. The rest of this is simply coding Unity style more-or-less (with an Udon twist)
Either way, it's still in alpha. More documentation will come. In the meantime, if you need to know how to do something, check Unity API reference. The vast majority of stuff is Unity, and the little bits that are VRChat specific actually aren't that many.
And Jasper, give your friend these links, have him use UdonSharp and the class browser to see what's exposed or not. He'll likely pick it up fairly quickly.
Also, join the discord. I, and others, will gladly help you and explain how to do things.
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCMLgCTDbjvOjMRsyLLbuuqw
https://github.com/Merlin-san/UdonSharp/wiki/vrchat-api
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/event-nodes
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/type-nodes
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/special-nodes
https://docs.vrchat.com/docs/whitelisted-world-components
https://7colou.red/UdonExternSearch/
https://docs.unity3d.com/2018.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/index.html
https://ask.vrchat.com/c/udon/5
https://ask.vrchat.com/t/spinning-cube-example-series/81

@{5e6dd8bb6326616c1b8214e2|full_name}: Just wanted to let you know that I myself need no help. I'd say I'm on the cutting edge with my Udon scripts and I'm using all available documentation to it's full extend, which means all of the above. But I appreciate your support. 
However, most of that "documentation" that is available is the result of reverse-engineering and guessing and we all agree that certain topics like networking are currently not behaving as they should (according to the available selfmade documentation). Thus, without a good documentation, we are left with try&error. 
What we would need is an inline-documentation which is a standard thing to have normally, this would avoid needing to search documentation together on several places and it also makes sense for VRChat to have that for themselves. A lack of inline-documentation is usually a sign of a missing basic structure in your coding style. No company (at least in the field where I work) would allow you to not have that. I'd excpect every exposed function (especially the custom ones) to have that. And since Udon does things different from Unity, we also need documentation for that. For example, you can't declare a negative float value in Udon since float values in Udons are something else compared to Unity/C#. Good luck finding this out and dealing with it :)

@{5c724f586a9e8a2255b7fc07|full_name}: My post was directed at Jasper Raine. You can see I mentioned Jasper's name in the post. I'm sorry if the system mistakenly tagged you and made it look like I sent that to you ;)
I corrected the tag to avoid further confusion. :)

@{5e6dd8bb6326616c1b8214e2|full_name}: I appreciate you trying to help, but truth is I'm not a programmer. I have a lot of trouble trying to understand programming of any sort. The main thing I want to bring to vrchat is some nice places to explore or hang out. With Udon I pretty much need a separate person that knows Udon in order to get anywhere with it. My friend I mentioned also does use Udon Sharp regularly as well as the documentation you've provided as well as their own research.

@{5cb0e62414ddd360bbe1ac29|full_name}: I'm going to have to agree with Reimajo on this. I think it has more to do with Udon itself than with programming. With other languages, there are enough, and clear examples, with clear API references that make it easy enough to understand if you put in the time and effort. But the current state of Udon seems to be confusion with regards to how to do anything. Me, very experienced with programming, had no clue at anything at first as well, and it wasn't without great effort to figure it out.
Anyways, if you ever need help, feel free to shoot me a message on Discord. I'd love to help out. IndominableRexxx#2978

details:
I know what I'm saying may sound ridiculous at first, but please hear me out.
As it stands right now, Udon is incredibly easy to use for people who know at least a little bit of programming and is definitely very powerful. However, for a person like myself, I have no idea what I'm doing! I can look at lots of tutorials for this, but in the end I'm ending up with a bunch of components that I have little to no idea of what they do and the only way I really know how to replicate things is if I take screen shots of what I've assembled or export them for later use. Right now I'm currently relying on a friend who has 3 years of programming experience in order to get anything done and when we were trying to get just a button and some doors to work, he basically, in his own words, went over 3 years of experience in just a day.
I think what Udon could use for people that just want to make some simple worlds without anything too complex is either more prefab scripts or an alternative mode that basically has things really dumbed down, perhaps even things that basically work as super nodes which serve the same functions as common functions used in scripts and worlds. Better documentation would also be very useful, and I'm aware that this section is currently under construction. I just feel like I'm going to be way behind everyone else if I keep using triggers since programming is way out of my skill range.
Please at the very least include more prefabs (And ones that actually work! The button prefab script doesn't actually work as of build 926.)
title: Udon is very difficult for world builders with no programming experience!
